# AI Disclosure

### I want to make it abundantly clear, this project was made with AI, and was majority generated by AI. 

**What was used:** [Claude](https://claude.ai), an AI assistant made by Anthropic
through its chat interface (Claude Sonnet 5.5 at the time of writing; later builds may use other Claude versions).

**What the AI did:** Claude analysed the upstream Rnote source code and wrote the modifications in this repository:
the changes to the code, installer and build scripts, the GitHub Actions workflow, and the documentation, including this README (With Amendments).
I thought of the features I wanted, and sometimes the problem solution avenues that could be taken/approaches to how certain features should be implemented and in what capacity. 
I run the builds, test the results and report problems back. 
I did not write the Rust code myself.
Claude cannot compile or run the app, so every build is only as well tested as I have managed to test it myself.
The unmodified upstream Rnote code was written by its own authors (see "License and credits" below).

## **A personal note:** 
I really enjoy learning and coding myself, and I believe AI has taken much of the fun and enjoyment out of
it for me by eliminating the creative problem-solving process, including my own unique thinking and perspective on solving problems.
(Yes, debugging AI-written code and prompt engineering are a form of creative problem solving, but for me they are not nearly as enjoyable.)

However, between my engineering studies and two part-time jobs, I can't afford to sink a significant amount of time into learning Rust
(my hobby coding has never touched it) or into developing this modification myself. Postponing it until I have more time is the obvious answer,
but I rely on Rnote for my note-taking and studying, which is why I can not simply 'slowly' learn and do this myself.

# Rnote-Mod

A personal, modified build of [Rnote](https://github.com/flxzt/rnote), the open-source infinite-canvas
drawing and note-taking app. Based on **Rnote 0.14.2**.

> **Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by the upstream Rnote project.**
> This is a personal fork made for private use. Please don't report problems with it to the Rnote developers.

## What this is

Rnote-Mod adds personal workflow tweaks (keyboard shortcuts, tool switching, and a colour pie menu) on top of
stock Rnote. Planned and finished changes are tracked in
[`rnote-mod_docs/rnote-mod_changelog.txt`](rnote-mod_docs/rnote-mod_changelog.txt), newest build first.
That file is the source of truth for what each build contains; this README does not list individual features.

It is **not** meant as a general, user-customisable replacement for Rnote.

Modified from Rnote 0.14.2 starting 2026-10-10. Each change, with its date, is listed in the changelog.

## Installs next to the original Rnote

Rnote-Mod uses its own installer ID, install folder (`Rnote-Mod`), application ID and settings location,
so it can be installed **alongside** a normal Rnote without overwriting it or sharing its settings.
Each new Rnote-Mod build installs over the previous Rnote-Mod build.

It does not take over `.rnote` files as the default program; it only appears under "Open with".

## Versions and naming

Feature builds are named `rnote-mod_vMAJOR-MINOR` (for example `rnote-mod_v1-1`); small fixes add a third number
(for example `rnote-mod_v1-0-1`). The version label is shown in Windows' installed apps list.

## Building (Windows installer)

You don't build locally. GitHub builds the installer on its own Windows machine:

1. Open the **Actions** tab of this repository.
2. Select **Build Rnote-Mod** → **Run workflow**.
3. Enter the build label (for example `v1-0`) and start the run.
4. When the run finishes, download the `rnote-mod_<label>` artifact from the run page. It contains the installer `.exe`.
   Artifacts are kept for 14 days.

The workflow is defined in `.github/workflows/build-rnote-mod.yml` and is started manually only.
Its build steps are the same as upstream Rnote's Windows release workflow.

To build locally instead, follow the upstream instructions in Rnote's `BUILDING.md`.

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `crates/` | Rnote source code (Rust): `rnote-compose`, `rnote-engine`, `rnote-ui`, `rnote-cli` |
| `build-aux/` | Build and installer scripts (the Inno Setup template holds the Rnote-Mod identity) |
| `.github/workflows/` | The manual build workflow |
| `rnote-mod_docs/` | Changelog and a map of the code structure |
